newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police say near goal in hunt for children.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police say near goal in hunt for children.

text.p: Belgian police hunting for a secret cell where convicted paedophile rapist Marc Dutroux may have kept some of his child victims, said on Tuesday they were convinced they were nearing their goal.

"We are not searching aimlessly. We are on the right track. We are near to the heart of the matter," Gendarmerie spokesman Guy Soumoy told reporters as police ended a fifth day of searching in the Jumet suburb of the central town of Charleroi.

Acting on statements by Dutroux and his second wife Michelle Martin, and on investigations of their own, police have been searching since Friday in an area of Jumet that is riddled with disused mineworkings.
They are certain that Dutroux, who once lived in a caravan near the site, used part of the old tunnels to hold kidnapped children.
A similar search of nearby old mineworkings in September on the basis of information from Dutroux proved fruitless.
On Tuesday 160 police minutely searched an area one kilometre square looking for sealed mine shafts and tunnels, marking two in particular for further investigation.
Belgium has been in a state of shock since mid-August when Dutroux and several alleged accomplices were arrested.
Police rescued two young girls from a secret dungeon in the basement of a house owned by Dutroux in the Marcinelle suburb of Charleroi. Both had been sexually abused.

Just two days later Dutroux led police to the bodies of two eight-year-old girls -- Julie Lejeune and Melissa Russo -- buried alongside that of a former Dutroux accomplice Bernard Weinstein in the garden of one of Dutroux' six homes in and around the town.
Dutroux has admitted killing Weinstein but the girls, missing for 14 months, had starved to death.

Less than three weeks later Dutroux led investigators to Weinstein's former house in Jumet where extensive digging unearthed the bodies of An Marchal and Eefje Lambrecks who had been missing for a year.
Police do not rule out the possibility of finding more bodies.
Dutroux, Martin, Michel Nihoul, Michel Lelievre and Mikael Diakostavrianos are still in prison while investigations continue.

Police, who are searching for at least another seven missing children, on Tuesday charged another man, Jacques Genevoix, in connection with the abduction in 1992 of a nine-year-old Moroccan girl, Loubna Benaissa. She is still missing.

A special parliamentary commission is investigating how Dutroux, released on parole in 1992 after serving just three years of a 13-year sentence for multiple child rape, managed to continue his activities undetected for so long.

Earlier this month Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck said that whatever the outcome of the current investigations into Dutroux, he would at the very least serve out the remainder of his earlier prison term.

The gendarmerie, which mounted its own surveillance operation on Dutroux codenamed "Othello" insists it passed all its findings to the judicial police and investigating magistrates. They deny all knowledge of the operation.
